agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider: addressing indoor heat in Burnaby rental units
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to hear a delegation from Michelle Ernst about addressing indoor heat in rental units. This is an information item only at this stage — no bylaw has been proposed yet. The purpose listed is to provide information on a Graffiti Strategy, which may be a separate or related topic. If you are a landlord or property manager, this could signal future rules about cooling requirements in rentals. If you are a tenant, this could affect your right to a cooler home in summer heat. Watch for next steps after this delegation.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision after this delegation — future cooling rules could affect rental properties.
agenda_briefs.source_body:
5.1 DELEGATION: Michelle Ernst - Addressing Indoor Heat in Rental Units
Purpose: To provide information on Graffiti Strategy.
agenda_briefs.article_title: Public Safety Committee Meeting Agenda — September 03, 2026

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider: Max Dixon Murdock requests maximum heat bylaw
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a delegation from Max Dixon Murdock requesting a maximum heat bylaw. This proposed bylaw would set a cap on indoor temperatures, likely to protect tenants and workers during extreme heat events. The request is up for discussion at an upcoming council meeting, but no decision has been made yet. If approved, it could affect landlords, property managers, and businesses that operate indoor spaces.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council meeting date and attend or submit comments to have your say on the proposed maximum heat bylaw.
agenda_briefs.industries: Landlord & Property Mgmt, Tenant, Labour & Employment

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider action on Burnaby rat problem
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider a request from Craig T. Wilson to take action on a rat problem in Burnaby. The delegation asks the city to address the issue, which could affect local businesses dealing with pest concerns. A proposed response or bylaw may be discussed at an upcoming meeting, but no decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on this delegation — it could affect how pest control is handled in your area.
agenda_briefs.industries: Food Service, Grocery & Food Retail, Landlord & Property Mgmt
agenda_briefs.source_body: 5.3 DELEGATION: Craig T. Wilson - A Request to Action to Solve a Rat Problem

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider new graffiti strategy for Burnaby
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to receive a verbal report on a proposed graffiti strategy. This is an information item, meaning Council will hear details about how the city plans to prevent and remove graffiti, but no decision has been made yet. The report is part of a broader effort to address property maintenance and community appearance. Business owners should be aware that future rules or programs could affect how they handle graffiti on their properties, but nothing is approved at this time.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Monitor the council meeting for details on the graffiti strategy — future rules could affect your property maintenance duties.
agenda_briefs.industries: Landlord & Property Mgmt, Retail, Construction & Development

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Burnaby RCMP report on FIFA 2026 response
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to receive a verbal report from the Burnaby RCMP Detachment about their response to the FIFA 2026 World Cup. The report is informational only — it will outline how local police prepared for and handled the event. No new rules or fees are proposed in this item, but the report may signal future decisions about policing costs or event planning that could affect local businesses.
agenda_briefs.action_required: No action needed now — monitor the council meeting for any follow-up motions on policing costs or event-related business impacts.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider RCMP status and performance plan reports
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to review a status update on local RCMP policing operations covering April to July 2026, along with the Annual Performance Plan quarterly report for April to June 2026. This is an informational update, not a decision on new rules. It may highlight trends in crime or community safety that could affect local businesses.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Review the reports when published to stay informed on local safety trends that may affect your business.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider: Burnaby Fire Department July 2026 status report
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to review the Fire Department's status report for July 2026 at its upcoming meeting. The report provides an update on the department's operations and activities through the end of July. This is an informational item for Council — no new rules or fees are proposed at this time. Business owners may want to be aware of any operational changes noted in the report, but no direct action is required.

No decisions have been made yet, but the update could signal upcoming changes that affect local businesses.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider: Safer Streets in the Heights proposal
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a proposal called 'Safer Streets in the Heights,' submitted by Sophia Oblitas Van Straten. The item was referred from the Community Planning Committee (CCP) meeting on August 25, 2026. This is a proposed initiative that could lead to changes in street design or traffic measures in the Heights neighbourhood, but no decision has been made yet. Council will review the correspondence and decide whether to move forward with any actions.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on this proposal — it could affect traffic and street access in the Heights area.
